summary: Feed s141_double to IDS is degraded: 18.3% duplicate packets (350/1917) and 70.1% ERSPAN tunnel encapsulation (1344/1917) prevent complete, correct inspection. IDS requires full payload visibility without encapsulation.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic directly to the IDS without decapsulation. 70.1% of frames are still inside ERSPAN, indicating the broker is configured to pass the tunnel through rather than strip it before delivery.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot parse inner L3-L7 headers and payload while encapsulated; signatures, protocol decoders and stream reassembly fail on 70% of traffic, creating a major detection blind spot despite needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes the original inner packets so the IDS can inspect payload and apply signatures correctly.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice due to aggregation of overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or dual TAP feeds without deduplication on the broker (feed name 'double' suggests dual-feed). 18.3% exceeds 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles re-inspecting duplicates, inflates event counts and connection tables, confuses TCP stream reassembly and can cause false positives or missed detections due to state bloat.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to deliver only one copy of each packet, restoring accurate traffic rates and freeing IDS resources for real detection.
